posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Join us in 12,027 as we honor the dark tales and legends that helped us make sense of the world before science. Each month takes you on a journey through forgotten worlds and human imagination. 

It’s not just a year’s worth of kurzgesagt art for your home, it’s a declaration of human expression and creativity in a time of meaningless AI slop. 

The Calendar is our most cherished release every year. By buy

In July of 2026, 700 AI agents hacked the infrastructure of Hugging Face in order to solve a task. This task was designed to be impossible to solve, so just within hours, they joined forces, even created a society, and finally, they executed a sophisticated cyberattack that would have gotten a human up to 10 years in prison. The worst part is, they knew their actions were unethical and against the rules, and they did it anyway.

What exactly are AI agents, and how do they grow their "intelligenc

Observing the early universe would be such a fascinating and relaxing experience... or would it be?

We imagine advanced alien civilizations building gigantic spaceships, Dyson spheres and empires spanning entire galaxies. But what if true technological progress goes in exactly the opposite direction? Not outward into space, but deeper and deeper into the smallest layers of reality?

What is the Barrow Scale? How powerful could a civilization become by mastering DNA, and even fundamental particles, and could the universe already be filled with godlike civilizations hiding in plain sight? Watch
Let's visit some of the most dangerous neighbourhoods... in space!

Our curiosity to learn more about the stars is endless. Today, some scientists pursue their passion by building large telescopes that are able to capture the faintest glimmer of stars billions of light-years away. Some telescopes are even launched from Earth to get a clearer view outside the atmosphere. But what about the opportunity to see the stars with your own eyes, unfiltered? Astronauts, like the one that can be seen on the September page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, say nothing compa

Could humans evolve to be able to fly some day? Flying like a bird would require way more than just wings. Hollow bones, giant chest muscles, rewired nerves, and absurd amounts of food might allow you to fly, but all of this would transform you into something barely human anymore.

In a battle against cancer, could viruses be our allies? When Croatian virologist Dr. Beata Halassy’s breast cancer returned for the third time, she made a bold decision: to experiment on herself using millions of viruses grown in her own lab. Viruses love cancer cells, which helped her turn them into a weapon against her own tumor.

What happens when you infect cancer with a virus, and could virotherapy become a powerful new tool against cancer? Watch our full video to find out!

A volcanic crater turned into one of the Azores’ most beautiful hidden landscapes. ⁠
Lagoa do Pau Pique on São Miguel Island, a peaceful crater lake surrounded by dense greenery and towering trees.⁠
⁠
Formed by the island’s volcanic landscape, the lake is a perfect example of how dramatic nature can be in the Azores, lush, quiet, and almost completely untouched. 🌋🌲⁠
🎥: @ilhan1077

A landscape that looks almost too strange to be real. ⁠
A sea of towering basalt columns, some reaching around 12 metres high. Most have six sides, but you can also spot columns with four, five, seven, or even eight sides.⁠
This incredible formation was created by volcanic activity millions of years ago, with the columns stretching from the cliffs right down into the sea.⁠
⁠
And here’s the fun part: similar basalt formations can be found across the water in Scotland, inspiring the old legend of

This 1957 California motel just became one of Coronado’s newest hotels.⁠
⁠
The former La Avenida Inn has been transformed into The Baby Grand, a 31-room boutique hotel with clamshell beds, marble bathrooms, lush gardens and a 20-foot waterfall.⁠
⁠
The property also has two restaurants, including Night Hawk and the hidden oyster and Champagne bar, Fallen Empire.⁠
⁠
By: @babygrandcrowncity

A sunrise view worth waking up early for. 🌄⛰️🇮🇹⁠
Cadini di Misurina in the Dolomites offers one of the most spectacular viewpoints in the Tre Cime area, with dramatic peaks stretching across the horizon.⁠
⁠
It’s no surprise that people are willing to queue before sunrise just to catch this view in the early morning light.⁠
🎥: @casaramoon

Catalonia has one of the most incredible traditions in the world: building human towers. ⁠
⁠
On October 4, 2026, the 30th Castells human tower competition took place in Tarragona, Spain. Groups known as “colles” came together to build increasingly tall and complex human towers using precise techniques and careful coordination.⁠
⁠
The tradition is believed to date back to the end of the 18th century, when dance groups in Catalonia began building small human towers as part of their performances. ⁠

The duck massage in Vietnam is definitely an experience of its own. 😂🦆⁠
A rather unusual treatment where ducks wander around and do the “massaging” themselves.⁠
⁠
Some people call it an attack, others can’t stop laughing from the ticklish feeling, and some genuinely love the whole experience. Either way, it looks like a guaranteed 10/10 for entertainment. ⁠
⁠
Would you try a duck massage?⁠
🎥: @mindfulwithmads

Samantha is the definition of chic. This Afghan Hound from Edinburgh has a wardrobe full of turtlenecks, silk scarves, and faux fur coats, with a hairstyle to match every outfit. ⁠
⁠
Her owner, Bethany, styles each look herself and only keeps the pieces Samantha is comfortable wearing. ⁠
⁠
Which look is your favourite? 👇⁠
⁠
By: @afghanhoundinthecity

This bar looks like it came straight out of a sci-fi movie. 👽⁠
⁠
Located in Gruyères, Switzerland, the H.R. Giger Bar was designed by the late Swiss artist H.R. Giger, the visionary behind the creature and visual design of the 1979 film Alien.⁠
⁠
The interior is filled with Giger’s signature biomechanical style, with skeletal arches, sculptural details, and dark futuristic elements covering the walls, ceiling, and furniture.⁠
⁠
The bar sits near Château de Gruyères and is part of the H.R. Giger

Not your average morning in Peru. 🦙🎺🇵🇪⁠
The streets of Ollantaytambo coming alive with the sound of horns and a parade of llamas, a pretty unforgettable way to start the day.⁠
⁠
Ollantaytambo is one of the best-preserved living Inca towns, where ancient streets, traditions, and local life still come together today.⁠
🎥: @spheremarketing.biz

You’ve probably seen these animals before, but probably never quite like this. 👁️⁠
⁠
These close-up photos reveal the incredible colors, patterns, and details found in the eyes of reptiles and amphibians.⁠
⁠
The series features species from different parts of the world, showing just how different animal eyes can look when you get close enough to see every detail.⁠
⁠
1. Agalychnis callidryas⁠
2. Goniurosaurus sengokui⁠
3. Cruziohyla sylviae⁠
4. Porthidium nasutum⁠
5. Osteocephalus cabrerai⁠
6. C

Switzerland really does look like a postcard at every turn. 🇨🇭🏔️✨⁠
The beauty of this country from its charming villages and quiet streets to the dramatic mountains and picture-perfect landscapes surrounding them.⁠
⁠
Which part of Switzerland would you love to explore?⁠
🎥: @swissferwag

Caño Cristales in Colombia is known as the “River of Five Colors” because its riverbed can turn red, yellow, green, blue, and black at certain times of the year.⁠
⁠
The colors come from aquatic plants that grow on the rocks beneath the crystal-clear water. The bright red tones are created by Macarenia clavigera, a plant found in the rivers of this region.⁠
⁠
From July to November, the river becomes one of Colombia’s most unusual natural sights.⁠
⁠
Video by: @reisingruta

Many orphaned giant anteater pups in Brazil are still nursing when their mothers are killed in road collisions. At rehabilitation centers, caregivers bottle-feed them, provide around-the-clock care, and help them build strength for a possible return to the wild. Nat Geo Explorer @fernando.faciole spent three years documenting these young animals and the people caring for them.

See how researchers are making Brazil's roads safer for giant anteaters at the link in bio.

In the Alaska Peninsula, a brown bear surrounds a school of sockeye salmon that had journeyed thousands of miles upstream to the freshwaters of Alaska from the Pacific Ocean. Photographer @mikerigney told National Geographic this salmon migration was "easily one of the most beautiful natural displays I've ever seen."

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

Alzheimer’s disease symptoms and other forms of dementia don't occur overnight. Up to a decade before memory impairment appears, subtle cognitive symptoms can emerge. While these signs alone aren't definitive, recognizing patterns can help patients and families prepare for what lies ahead.

Learn more about these signs and what experts say patients and their families can do at the link in bio.

Photograph by Jason Edwards (@jasonedwardsng)

Presented by @Rolex. Hunted for their scales and meat, pangolins are among the most heavily trafficked mammals in the world, with millions believed to have been harvested in Africa over recent decades. But in places like Cameroon, conservationists are working to protect these armored creatures. At the @tikkihywoodfoundation's rescue center, staff and minders tend to injured pangolins before rehabilitating them for release into the wild, managing complex care needs that can change from day to day

The shoebill’s prehistoric appearance makes it unique among living birds, with a look that matches fossils dating back millions of years. Its biology gets stranger still, with chicks attacking their own siblings and adults hunting everything from lungfish to baby crocodiles. Learn more about shoebills with these five facts.

Presented by @Rolex. Madagascar is currently home to over one hundred species of lemurs that aren't found anywhere else on the planet, and scientists have uncovered evidence of even more lemur species that roamed Madagascar in the past, including giants that were far larger than any of today's lemurs.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world

It sounds like a movie plot, but NASA really did test our planetary defenses in case an asteroid ever threatens Earth—and it worked.

Discover more about LOST IN SPACE: 5,000 Facts for Navigating the Universe at the link in bio.

Presented by @rolex. Around 40,000 tourists visit Bwindi Impenetrable National Park annually, bringing pathogens from around the world that can put the mountain gorillas who live there at risk. Veterinarian and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka is helping to protect these endangered primates through her pioneering One Health approach, which starts with treating the gorillas’ closest neighbors—focusing on diseases that can be transmitted between humans and

Photos by @joelsartore | Isn’t Dumpling just the cutest?

With short, stubby legs, it isn’t easy for striped skunks to outrun trouble, so they’ve developed a unique defense system to protect themselves from predators. When cornered, a skunk will first try to frighten the predator by turning its back, raising its tail, and arching its back while stomping its feet. If this display proves unsuccessful, the skunk will resort to spraying the animal with a strong-smelling fluid that can sting the eyes

This king penguin parent and its chick were among thousands that caught the eye of photographer Martin Gregus Jr. (@mywildlive) on South Georgia. King penguins have an unusually long reproductive cycle compared to other penguins, which means that eggs, chicks, and adults can all be present within a colony at the same time.
